hypothesis: With a cache slot for every expert and the model in the page cache, a fresh qwen36 server's first replies are slow because each expert's first use reads and repacks it on the engine's thread; filling the free slots from background threads at startup (Q36_PRELOAD=1) should bring the first replies to the warm speed and shorten the first token, with the same text and no cost once warm.
model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kreuzzelg/qwen36-35b-a3b-colibri-i4-gs64 (int4 gs=64 safetensors container from the one-step setup)
command: make -C c qwen36 ARCH=native; python3 docs/experiments/qwen36-preload-2026-11-17/bench.py MODEL OUT off:WT/c on:WT/c:Q36_PRELOAD=1, three times (each run: coli serve --model MODEL --auto-tier --port 8011, with the preload wait for its 'experts loaded' line, one warm-up request, three timed requests, five others, the same three again; tok_s holds the FIRST round, which is what the preload changes); racing.txt: race:WT/c:Q36_PRELOAD=1,NOWAIT=1 twice

hardware.cpu: 2x Intel Xeon E5-2670 (Sandy Bridge-EP: AVX, SSSE3, no AVX2, no FMA, no F16C), 16 cores / 32 threads, 2 NUMA nodes
hardware.ram: 94 GiB DDR3, 64 GB on node 0 and 32 GB on node 1
hardware.storage: 7200 rpm HDD, ext4 (rw,relatime); the model was in the page cache for every run

config.BUILD: make qwen36 ARCH=native, GCC 15.2.1, binary sha256 605560d91ba116e3c89457c94a4c1c978c7b7c4b921d611c86560a91b18a1da1

quality.method: tests/test_qwen36_preload.py passes (the replies of the tiny fixtures are the ones without the preload, racing the loaders and after them, caps 8 and 2, 1/4/16 loaders); the text of the six timed replies is byte-identical in all eight runs, the two racing ones included (sha256 9ec0f3c7a6ffae4888f65424209f872fb43178efcb3d64132ef3cb1d007d58eb)
